title: Damon Chen: From Cisco engineer to $1.3M ARR across Testimonial and PDF.ai
summary: Damon Chen recounts leaving Cisco after four failed side projects to build Testimonial to $800K+ ARR alone, then PDF.ai to $500K+. The free portion covers launching on Product Hunt, product-led growth loops, an affiliate program, buying a typo domain, and negotiating the risk with his wife. The PDF.ai growth channels are paywalled.

principles.text: Reuse existing code and ship fast: a failed project's codebase can become the next product.
principles.quote: It used about 80% of the same code as Indielog. I just added a landing page and Stripe payments before launching it on Product Hunt

principles.text: Launch with lifetime deals to get early cash and validation before moving to subscriptions.
principles.quote: I was selling lifetime access for $199. I sold 30 deals and generated $6K in revenue in the first two weeks.

principles.text: Engineers who dislike marketing can lean on product-led growth: let the product's output carry a branded link back to signup.
principles.quote: I’m an engineer who doesn’t know much about marketing or sales. Instead, I focused on product-led growth.

principles.text: A branded badge on free output is both a growth loop and an upgrade incentive.
principles.quote: The testimonial logo also incentivized people to upgrade to the paid plan to remove it.

principles.text: A generous recurring-commission affiliate program can drive a meaningful share of revenue.
principles.quote: gives anyone who signs up a paid customer 30% commission every month. The customer also gets 15% off for the first year. This program contributes about 10-15% of our total revenue.

principles.text: Buying the look-alike domain people mistakenly visit can pay back: $35K on testimonial.io returned $80K lifetime.
principles.quote: I realized that many people mistakenly visited testimonial.io instead of testimonial.to. So I spent $35,000 to buy the .io domain.
